proposed_widenings.name: Duration.until_reactivated
proposed_widenings.justification: The Portable Hole's open state persists until the bearer explicitly closes it with a second Magic action. No existing Duration variant captures 'active until the owning activation is explicitly ended by a second activation on the same item'. The closest variants (timed, concentration, permanent) all end on natural expiry or dispel, not on a deliberate second-activation close.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You can take a Magic action to unfold a Portable Hole and place it on or against a solid surface... You can take a Magic action to close a Portable Hole by taking hold of the edges of the cloth and folding it up.

proposed_widenings.name: ContainerStorageProfile without mandatory maxWeightPounds
proposed_widenings.justification: The SRD gives no weight capacity for the Portable Hole — only physical dimensions (6 ft diameter cylinder, 10 ft deep). ContainerStorageProfile requires maxWeightPounds, which would force fabricating a value not in the source text. A variant with an optional or absent weight limit is needed to represent items whose only capacity constraint is geometric/physical.
proposed_widenings.evidence: No matter what's in it, the hole weighs next to nothing. (No stated weight limit for contents; only physical dimensions constrain what can fit.)

proposed_widenings.name: toggle_activated_container
proposed_widenings.justification: The Portable Hole is fundamentally a two-activation toggle: one activation opens the extradimensional space (giving it container_storage semantics for that session) and a second activation closes it. The current surface has no family for 'activation whose effect persists until a second paired activation ends it'. This differs from both passive (always-on) and standard activation (instantaneous or duration-expiring). A composite of two activations cannot express the pairing relationship, and attaching container_storage to one activation phase but not the other has no lifecycle semantics in the current model.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You can take a Magic action to unfold a Portable Hole... You can take a Magic action to close a Portable Hole by taking hold of the edges of the cloth and folding it up. Folding the cloth closes the hole, and any creatures or objects within remain in the extradimensional space.

proposed_widenings.name: OngoingTrigger.on_creature_inside_spends_action (or container escape mechanic)
proposed_widenings.justification: The escape mechanic fires when a creature INSIDE the closed container spends its action, resolving as an ability_check_gate (DC 10 STR Athletics). No existing OngoingTrigger variant covers 'creature contained within this item's storage space takes an action'. This is distinct from on_creature_studies (which targets the attachment, not a creature inside it) and from all existing turn/damage/movement triggers.
proposed_widenings.evidence: If the hole is folded up, a creature within the hole's extradimensional space can take an action to make a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check. On a successful check, the creature forces its way out and appears within 5 feet of the Portable Hole.

proposed_widenings.name: extradimensional_interaction_destruction
proposed_widenings.justification: The rule 'placing one extradimensional item inside another destroys both and opens a planar gate' is a two-item interaction trigger with no surface analogue. It requires: detecting the extradimensional context of the target container, destroying both items simultaneously, opening a transport_exile gate to the Astral Plane originating at the placement point, and affecting nearby creatures with a forced-movement-into-exile effect with a reach check. No existing trigger, phase, or lifecycle atom expresses item-item extradimensional collision.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Placing a Portable Hole inside an extradimensional space created by a Bag of Holding, Handy Haversack, or similar item instantly destroys both items and opens a gate to the Astral Plane. Any creature within 10 feet of the gate and not behind Total Cover is sucked through it and deposited in a random location on the Astral Plane.

notes: The toggle-open/close pattern is the structural blocker. Unlike Bag of Holding (always-open passive container), Portable Hole requires two activations to manage state. container_storage, alter_item_kind, ability_check_gate, and transport_exile all exist as atoms; the gap is purely at the surface/family level: no lifecycle shape for 'activation that persists until a second paired activation ends it', and ContainerStorageProfile requires maxWeightPounds which the SRD does not provide for this item.
